introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Mechanics Paper 2 (0765/2), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2024. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.

questions.enonce_markdown: Solve the differential equation $x\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y(y+1)$, given that $y = 4$, when $x = 2$ and express the solution in the form $y = f(x)$. (7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The variables separate:

$$\frac{dy}{y(y+1)} = \frac{dx}{x}.$$

Partial fractions: $\dfrac{1}{y(y+1)} = \dfrac1y - \dfrac{1}{y+1}$. Integrate both sides:

$$\ln|y| - \ln|y+1| = \ln|x| + c \;\Longrightarrow\; \ln\left|\frac{y}{y+1}\right| = \ln|x| + c \;\Longrightarrow\; \frac{y}{y+1} = Ax,$$

where $A$ is a constant ($A = \pm e^c$). Use $y = 4$ when $x = 2$: $\dfrac45 = 2A$, so $A = \dfrac25$. Hence

$$\frac{y}{y+1} = \frac{2x}{5} \;\Longrightarrow\; 5y = 2x(y + 1) \;\Longrightarrow\; y(5 - 2x) = 2x.$$

$$\boxed{y = \frac{2x}{5 - 2x}}$$

(valid on the branch containing $x = 2$, that is for $x < \tfrac52$.)

Check: at $x = 2$, $y = \dfrac{4}{1} = 4$. Differentiating, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2(5 - 2x) + 4x}{(5 - 2x)^2} = \dfrac{10}{(5 - 2x)^2}$, and $\dfrac{y(y+1)}{x} = \dfrac{2x}{5 - 2x}\cdot\dfrac{5}{5 - 2x}\cdot\dfrac1x = \dfrac{10}{(5 - 2x)^2}$, as required.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Using a suitable substitution, show that

$$\int_0^2 x\sqrt{1 + x^2}\,dx = \frac13\left(5\sqrt5 - 1\right).$$

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $u = 1 + x^2$. Then $du = 2x\,dx$, so $x\,dx = \dfrac12 du$. Limits: $x = 0 \Rightarrow u = 1$; $x = 2 \Rightarrow u = 5$.

$$\int_0^2 x\sqrt{1 + x^2}\,dx = \frac12\int_1^5 u^{1/2}\,du = \frac12\left[\frac{2}{3}u^{3/2}\right]_1^5 = \frac13\left(5^{3/2} - 1^{3/2}\right).$$

Since $5^{3/2} = 5\sqrt5$,

$$\int_0^2 x\sqrt{1 + x^2}\,dx = \frac13\left(5\sqrt5 - 1\right). \qquad \blacksquare$$

(Numerically $\dfrac13(11.1803 - 1) = 3.3934$.)
